item.title: Slender defeat for Millwall Lionesses
item.description: Millwall Lionesses were beaten 1-0 by Dartford on Sunday afternoon. A goal for the hosts in the 68th minute saw Ted Jones' side slip to a first loss in five matches. Madison Grandys made a second Lionesses debut shortly after the goal after re-joining the club earlier last week. Millwall: Deans, Jones, Lockett, Butler, Joyce, Helt, Squirrell, Bussey, Richards, Winfield, Throp. Subs: Buddle-Smith, Coldrick, Grandys, Edwards, Abu.FixturesDartford Vs. Millwall - Sun, Feb 22 2026, 13:00

item.title: Record 'New' Den League attendance broken for second time in 2025/26
item.description: Millwall Football Club's record League attendance at The 'new' Den' was broken for a second time in a matter of weeks last Saturday. With the record standing at 19,004 following the win over Charlton Athletic on 24th January, a total of 19,153 supporters packed into SE16 as The Lions took on Portsmouth this past weekend, raising the bar by a further 149 fans. item.title: Millwall duo visit Bacon's College
item.description: Millwall First-Team duo Lukas Jensen and Daniel Kelly visited Bacons College today as part of Millwall Community Trust’s Post-16 Football & Education Academy. Millwall Community Trust offers a unique opportunity for passionate 16-18-year-olds football players, both male and female, to pursue a two-year Football & Education Scholarship - this course is run at Bacons College as well as other educational sites. Also in attendance throughout the afternoon was Millwall Community Trust CEO, Sean Daly.

item.title: Nugent's take on Bournemouth defeat
item.description: Under 21s manager Kevin Nugent spoke to millwallfc.co.uk following Monday’s 4-0 Professional Development League defeat to AFC Bournemouth. Nugent’s initial assessment of the performance was that "we started the game OK and had the bulk of the opportunities, good opportunities which we didn’t take." He added that "after the first 20/25 minutes, they dominated the game, with a couple of opportunities and they took them. It wasn’t the best of defending from us; they grew and grew and we didn’t." item.title: Mixed fortunes for Lions loanees
item.description: There were mixed fortunes for Millwall's loanees this past weekend. On a positive note, Wes Harding's spell at Plymouth Argyle went from strength-to-strength as The Green Army thumped promotion-chasing Cardiff City 5-2 in Sky Bet League One. After a breathless 15-minute period at the end of the first-half saw five goals scored - and Plymouth go in 3-2 up at the break - Harding assisted Plymouth's third goal in the win.
